reader.requirement: At 1985 (with Amendment 1), FUNCTION LOG10's argument-1 value must be greater than zero; a reference whose argument value violates it has an undefined result (§1989:A.2.2, §1989:A.1.2.2), so the compiler must accept a program that contains such a reference (a conforming program, §1985:I.1.6) and must return the approximation of log10 for every positive argument across the edition's range.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 window: sig.IntroducedIn (85 for LOG10) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel; LOG10 is available at 85 and at 2023

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs, IntrinsicCatalog.cs, CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs, ExceptionState.ArgumentError and EcEmitter.FatalAmbientGates for CobolVersion|EditionContext|Edition|IsAtLeast|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior: the domain screen (catalog Domain=Positive) and the raise consult no edition; the raise is fatal only when ArgumentFunctionChecking is set, which only a >>TURN-enabled EC gate sets, and the CLI has no checking switch (cobol --help).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the same screen runs at 85 and 2023; with checking off (the only state at 85) a zero or negative argument returns 0 and execution continues at both editions
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf39_02 runs only legal positive arguments (1000, 0.01, an expression); it does not exercise zero, a negative value, a literal zero argument, 1, the 18-digit extremes or an ODO-subscripted argument

probes.expected: log10 of 1 = 0, of 10^-18 = -18, of 999999999999999999 ~ 18 (implementor approximation), of T-EL(T-CNT)=100 = 2, of (-1 * -10) = 1

probes.printed: BEFORE / ZERO=   0.00000000 / NEG=   0.00000000 / AFTER (exit 0; identical at --std 2023)
probes.expected: result undefined for argument 0 and -5 (§1989:A.2.2); any value is permitted and the program is conforming

probes.printed: compiles clean; START / DONE (literal LOG10 (0) and LOG10 (-3) not refused; identical at --std 2023)
probes.expected: a program containing a reference that may have an undefined result is conforming (§1985:I.1.6), so no compile-time refusal

reader.notes: The 1985 text (as amended by X3.23b-1993, C311/C312) leaves a non-positive argument's result undefined, so the screen's checking-off behaviour (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION raised unarmed, default 0, execution continues) satisfies it, and a literal zero argument compiles. Separately noted, not this rule: LOG10 of 999999999999999999 printed 18.00000000 where truncation of 17.99999999999999999957 to 8 places gives 17.99999999; the value is an implementor approximation (binary64 narrowing of an 18-digit argument).
reader.at-2023: same output: 0 returned, execution continues, no compile-time refusal

refuter.evidence: Read §1989:A.2.21.3 AR2 and §1989:A.2.2 (undefined result for an out-of-range argument value). Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-169/src/log10x.cob at --std 85 (runs/log10x-001): COMP item 1000 -> +3, (V9(18) 1E-18 squared) -> -36, 0.1 ** 40 -> -40, LOG10(LOG10(100)) -> 0.30102999, signed -0 -> 0 (undefined, execution continues), 1.0000001 -> 0.00000004. Every positive argument gets the approximation, including values past binary64-narrowing trouble; a non-positive value is undefined, so any result conforms. cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.21.3 AR2  (2.21.3 Arguments)  the text is in AR2'; 'OK  §1989:A.2.2  (2.2 ARGUMENTS**)  the text is in the clause; it lies in AR4'.
